actions.assumptions_changed: Moving away from hyper-rational equilibrium models toward path-dependent multi-agent reinforcement learning mechanisms.
actions.new_frame: Complex, large-scale conventions and divergent preference equilibria can emerge dynamically from model-free reinforcement learning under taste heterogeneity and path dependence.
actions.old_frame: Preferences are strictly determined by initial hyper-parameters and global common knowledge.
actions.reason: Aligns project scope with empirical reinforcement learning literature on multi-agent coordination.
actions.strategy: Examine how local interactions and historical path dependence fracture symmetric initial states into distinct preference equilibria.
actions.trigger: Literature evidence demonstrating convention emergence via model-free reinforcement learning.

review.alternative: Conventions might rely entirely on explicit model-based planning and common knowledge rather than habit-like reinforcement learning.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration that model-free agents fail to form stable conventions in temporo-spatially extended games.

claims.statement: Complex, large-scale conventions and stable preference patterns can emerge from model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning mechanisms.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that model-free reinforcement learning is sufficient to generate large-scale conventions and structured coordination.
support.passage: Here, we demonstrate that complex, large-scale conventions can emerge from MF learning mechanisms. This suggests that some conventions may be supported by habit-like cognition rather than explicit reasoning.

actions.findings: Complex, large-scale conventions and stable preference patterns can emerge from model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning mechanisms. [source-e95a205c9be74729]
actions.limitations: Simulated game-theoretic environments may not fully capture open-ended real-world moral and value evolution.
actions.next_questions: How do variations in initial stochastic seeds alone (absent intrinsic taste heterogeneity) affect the specific equilibrium reached by identical reinforcement learning agents?
actions.reason: Synthesizes retrieved literature on convention formation and taste heterogeneity into an initial formal notebook.
actions.summary: Examines how model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning allows distinct subgroups to settle into different equilibria, providing a mechanism for value divergence from symmetric starting points.
actions.title: Path Dependence and Convention Emergence in Multi-Agent Systems
